marks.gloss_en: מתיב רב אושעיא: one who detaches from a perforated pot is liable, from an unperforated one exempt -- what does not grow from the ground is not 'uprooted from its place of growth'
התם לאו היינו רביתיה, הכא היינו רביתיה -- an unperforated pot is not where a plant grows; a jug handle is where a mushroom grows (= p_hatam_lav_rbitei)
Abaye: one who detaches a mushroom from the handle of a jug is liable on account of uprooting a thing from its place of growth
[איכא דאמרי] אף אנן נמי תנינא: 'by its wings' -- to include the skin; granted if it is skin, that is why a verse was needed to include it; if not skin, why a verse?
לעולם אימא לך לאו עור הוא, ואיצטריך: you would think, since it has many breaches it is repulsive -- it teaches us (= p_abaye_lav_or, p_abaye_itztrich_pirtzei)
the baraita (as the איכא דאמרי recites it): 'by its wings' -- to include the skin
[first tradition] מיתיב רבי זירא: 'by its wings' -- to validate the skin; if it is skin, how does the verse include it?
עור הוא ורחמנא רבייה -- it is skin, and the Merciful One included it (= p_abaye_or_verachmana_rabbeih)
the baraita: 'by its wings' (Lev 1:17) -- to validate the skin
הא חזינן דאית ליה עור -- we see that it has skin
ועוד, התנן: עצמות הדג ועורו מצילין באהל המת -- the mishna speaks of a fish's skin
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: if Elijah comes and says
Rav Yosef: that a bird has skin, we have already learned
תנינא: החובל בהן חייב -- the mishna makes one liable for wounding a bird, so a bird has skin
the mishna: one may not make brine [heilmei] on Shabbat
'orlato' of circumcision / 'orlato' of fruit trees: as there a thing that bears fruit, so here
the stam: [this is] like the tannaim -- Rav's derivation is R' Yoshiya's, in a tannaitic dispute
דכתיב למען תהיה תורת ה' בפיך -- the source he gives for the rule that tefillin are not written on a non-kosher hide (kind svara stands in: no kind names a דכתיב derivation)
אלא מעתה, על גבי עור נבלות וטרפות אל יכתבו -- if only what is permitted in the mouth, then [tefillin] should not be written on nevelot and tereifot [which may not be eaten]
the parable of the two condemned men: the one the king killed is more praiseworthy (= p_mashal_harago_melech)
אלא מעתה יאכלו -- if so, let them [nevelot and tereifot] be eaten
התורה אמרה לא תאכלו כל נבלה (Deut 14:21) ואת אמרת יאכלו? -- the Torah forbade eating them explicitly; the Boethusian answers קאלוס
R' Yehoshua HaGarsi: as it is written 'that the Torah of the Lord may be in your mouth' (Ex 13:9) -- from a thing permitted in your mouth
Rav: 'orlato' is said here and 'orlato' there; as there [the tree] a thing that bears fruit, so here a thing that bears fruit
נאמר כאן ערלתו (Lev 12:3) ונאמר להלן ערלתו (Lev 19:23): as there [the tree] a thing that bears fruit, so here a thing that bears fruit
Karna: say his heart, as it is written 'and circumcise the foreskin of your heart' (Deut 10:16)
דנין ערלתו תמה מערלתו תמה, ואין דנין ערלתו תמה מערלתו שאינה תמה -- one derives a complete 'orlato' from a complete 'orlato', not from one that is not complete
Karna: say his ear, as it is written 'behold, their ear is uncircumcised' (Jer 6:10)
the same rule: a complete 'orlato' is not derived from a word that is not complete
tefillin are written on the hide of a kosher domestic animal and on the hide of a kosher wild animal
Shmuel and Karna were sitting on the bank of the Malka river; they saw the water rising and turning murky
Rav: what is your name? -- Karna. -- may it be [God's] will that a horn come out in his eye
in the end Shmuel brought him into his house, fed him barley bread and small fried fish, gave him beer to drink, and did not show him the privy, so that he would be loosened
